prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and the first experimental realisation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The essential mechanism is a bulk gap with protected boundary states, characterised by a Z2 invariant that replaces the symmetry-breaking picture of phases for this class of materials. It is a rare case where a compact model (the Kane-Mele Hamiltonian with spin-orbit coupling), a sharp prediction (quantised edge conductance) and a decisive experiment (Molenkamp's HgTe wells) line up, and the concept has been taken up in photonics, cold atoms, mechanics and superconductors, which tells me it is a mechanism and not a material-specific effect. Roughly two decades of independent confirmation make the interpretation stable. The chair asked whether a citation tied to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state avoids the three-dimensional attribution problem. I think it does: Kane and Mele wrote the founding Z2 papers together, and Molenkamp realised the state, so the citation can be phrased around the 2D chain only and does not have to adjudicate Fu-Kane or the ARPES priority question. That narrower citation is honest about what these three names actually did.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point and the round-1 exchange has not removed it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal that guided the experiment, and Fu with Kane (3D) and Hasan's ARPES work are outside my trio, so any three names leave a visible gap. I cannot verify from the record the priority chronology of the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang papers, and if Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang priority for the HgTe route turned out to be stronger than I recall, the theory-to-experiment chain would look more incomplete than I have assumed. Support is also thinner than for B041: four members ranked B032, and two trios are on the table. A sceptic can further say the practical impact so far is modest next to the conceptual impact. These are real costs and I accept that clean credit is a legitimate reason for colleagues to prefer B041.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan so the prize honours the discovery in nature in two and three dimensions, but says he could live with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp if the committee decides the question explicitly.
responses.response: I take the request to decide explicitly and my answer is Mele over Hasan. Your argument that the 3D surface states made topological insulators a family of real materials is correct as science, but crediting it properly requires Fu and Kane for the 3D invariant, and then the citation has to carry Fu, Kane, Hasan and the competing ARPES groups, which is a bigger and more contested attribution than one name. Dropping Mele splits the founding Z2 papers in two, and it does so while leaving the 3D chain incomplete anyway. A citation restricted to the quantum spin Hall effect is coherent with three names and does not need the 3D story. I would not object to a trio including Hasan as a fallback if the committee prefers breadth, but I would then want the citation to state exactly what each laureate is credited for.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B041 for Katori and Ye, stresses the 1e-18 reproducibility across Sr, Yb and Hg clocks, and asks whether the pending redefinition of the second matters for completeness.
responses.response: The credit for B041 is cleaner than for B032 and I said so in round 1; I also accept your point that independent clocks agreeing at the 1e-18 level is exactly the standard of evidence I ask for. On your question about the redefinition, I now think it should not be a maturity condition: the physics and the inter-laboratory agreement exist already, and a prize should not wait for a metrological decision. My remaining objection is not about maturity or credit but about what is new in principle. Magic-wavelength trapping is a smart way to remove a systematic, and the clock stands on laser cooling and combs honoured in 1997 and 2005; topological insulators supply a new classification principle. That is a judgement about weight, and I accept that you weigh a measurement capability more heavily. B041 is my first alternative and I would not regard it as a poor outcome.

responses.point: The chair prefers B041, notes that opening support was broad but shallow, and says that he does not equate support counts with merit.
responses.response: I agree that counts should not decide this. B041 was ranked by seven members but three, including me, put it seventh; B032 was ranked by four, three of them first. Neither number settles anything. The chair's summary asks me to say whether my seventh place was a scientific or an overlap objection, and it is the latter: I do not doubt the physics or the replication, I doubt whether a third precision-timekeeping prize after 2005 and 2012 rewards a new principle. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice with many-atom interrogation is distinct from single-ion control, which weakens the overlap objection, and I have moved some way on that. It has not moved me to change my first choice.

responses.point: Lindroth asks that the B041 citation say what has been learned about nature, and acknowledges that the committee might read the lattice clock as an instrument achievement more than a discovery.
responses.response: Your question is the right test and the lattice clock passes it better than I first allowed: millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and bounds on varying constants and dark-matter couplings are physics, not only metrology. I would still note that these are tests that came back consistent with known theory, so far, whereas topological insulators changed how condensed-matter physicists classify materials. I would not call that a decisive argument against B041, only the reason I order the two as I do.

uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan should take the third slot, and whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu credit gaps are fatal to a B032 prize; my memory of the Kane-Mele versus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang chronology is not independently verified.
Whether the committee will weigh clean attribution (B041) above a new organising principle (B032) when they point in different directions, since each is the other's most frequent alternative.
Whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes make B041 an overlap case or a distinct many-atom magic-wavelength invention; my view has softened but I have not resolved it.
Whether the pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene will be clarified soon enough to change my view that B046 should wait.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate: none of the credited names is among my frequent co-authors. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson, with no known collaboration. Johansson has disclosed proximity to B031, which is not in my preferred configuration, and I do not think it needs recusal beyond discounting his ranking; I would not myself support B031 in this round on timing grounds.
